stem.en: An earthworm and a beetle both have segmented bodies, but only the beetle has a hard external skeleton. How does this skeleton help the beetle survive?

text.en: It removes the need for muscles, because the hard covering moves the legs by itself.

feedback.en: The muscles still do the work. The hard covering supports them.

text.en: It lets water pass in from damp soil, so the beetle never has to find water.

feedback.en: The covering reduces water loss. It does not take water in.

text.en: It lets the body grow without limit, because the covering stretches with it.

feedback.en: The covering is rigid, so it does not stretch with the body.

text.en: It protects the body, reduces water loss and supports powerful muscles.

feedback.en: Right. These three jobs help arthropods survive in dry and exposed places.

explanation.en: A hard outer skeleton protects the body, reduces water loss and supports powerful muscles, so arthropods can survive in dry and exposed places.

hints.en: Think about what a hard, dry covering does in a dry place.
